## Findings
- claim-1: In the bounded \(a=1,b=2\) box/Pieri setting defined below, the Schur columns and all generators of the Pieri-row lattice are complete in degrees \(d+1\) and \(d+2\).
- claim-2: For \(p=c=1\), the degree-\(d+2\) row matrix, with rows \((2),(3),(4)\) and columns \((x_2,z,y_2)\), is \[ \begin{pmatrix}0&1&1\\1&1&0\\0&1&1\end{pmatrix}. \] Its rows \((2),(3)\) on columns \((z,y_2)\) form \[ \begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad\det=-1. \]
## Strategy
Work under the stipulated integral box/Pieri presentation. Put
\[
q=n-r,\quad p=q-i,\quad c=r-j,\quad d=ij,
\]
with \(a=1,b=2\); thus \(i,j\ge2\), \(p,c\ge1\), \(\min(p,c)=1\), and hence \(q,r\ge3\). Let
\[
x_0=s_{i^j}.
\]
The complete Schur-column lists in the relevant degrees are:
\[
J_{d+1}=\mathbb Zx_1\oplus\mathbb Zy_1,
\quad
x_1=s_{(i+1,i^{j-1})},\quad y_1=s_{(i^j,1)},
\]
and
\[
J_{d+2}=\mathbb Zu\oplus\mathbb Zx_2\oplus\mathbb Zz
 \oplus\mathbb Zy_2\oplus\mathbb Zw,
\]
after deleting
\[
u=s_{(i+2,i^{j-1})}\quad\text{if }p=1,\qquad
w=s_{(i^j,1,1)}\quad\text{if }c=1,
\]
where
\[
x_2=s_{((i+1)^2,i^{j-2})},\quad
z=s_{(i+1,i^{j-1},1)},\quad
y_2=s_{(i^j,2)}.
\]
These lists follow by adding respectively one or two boxes to \(i^j\), subject precisely to the \(q^r\)-box boundary.

The Pieri rows are
\[
h_1x_0=x_1+y_1,
\]
and, in degree \(d+2\),
\[
h_2x_0=u+z+y_2,\qquad
h_1x_1=u+x_2+z,\qquad
h_1y_1=z+y_2+w,
\]
with absent boundary columns omitted.

Since \(J_k=0\) for \(k<d\),
\[
(A_+J)_{d+1}=A_1J_d,\qquad
(A_+J)_{d+2}=A_2J_d+A_1J_{d+1}.
\]
Integrally,
\[
A_1=\mathbb Zh_1,\qquad
A_2=\mathbb Zh_2+\mathbb Zh_1^2,
\]
because \(q,r\ge3\) and
\[
h_2=s_{(2)},\qquad h_1^2=s_{(2)}+s_{(1,1)};
\]
the change-of-basis determinant relative to \((s_{(2)},s_{(1,1)})\) is \(1\). Moreover,
\[
h_1^2x_0=(h_1x_1)+(h_1y_1).
\]
Hence the displayed degree-\(d+2\) rows generate all of
\((A_+J)_{d+2}\), while \(h_1x_0\) generates all of
\((A_+J)_{d+1}\). Thus row completeness follows from the homogeneous-component equalities, not merely from minors.

For \(p=c=1\), the surviving degree-\(d+2\) columns are
\((x_2,z,y_2)\), and the three rows are
\[
\begin{pmatrix}
0&1&1\\
1&1&0\\
0&1&1
\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Rows \((2),(3)\) on \((z,y_2)\) give
\[
\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix},
\qquad\det=-1.
\]
This explicitly covers the doubly-boundary case.

## Gaps
The certificate is conditional on the stipulated integral box/Schur-basis presentation of \(A\), the stated Schur description of \(J\), and integral Pieri multiplication. No global elimination, higher-degree assertion, generation result, or parent-theorem conclusion is supplied.

## Next
Under those stipulated presentation hypotheses, the bounded certificate—completeness of the columns and Pieri rows in degrees \(d+1\) and \(d+2\)—is established.
